source: bolade2015 (cowpea trypsin inhibitor fell only 5.8 to 11.2 % after the first soak, 25.6 to 32.9 % after soak, dehull, soak, and to zero after steaming, frying or pressure cooking, four varieties); rizvi2024 (lima bean trypsin inhibitor was still 3.22 after 72 h germination against 20.41 raw); ijarotimi2022 introduction (anti-nutritional compounds are thermolabile). The app states no numeric cook time.
text: Soaking, dehulling, milling or sprouting alone does not remove the heat-sensitive anti-nutrients (trypsin inhibitors). Do not present a soak-only, sprout-only or raw-flour preparation as ready to eat. Cook bean and groundnut preparations until they are fully done.
user_text: Soaking, sprouting or milling alone is not enough. Always cook beans and groundnuts until fully soft.

source: WHO, Mycotoxins fact sheet, https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/mycotoxins ("discard any that look mouldy, discoloured, or shrivelled"; "Most mycotoxins are chemically stable and survive food processing"). Reviewer: decide whether to widen applies_to to all dry seeds.
text: Discard groundnuts, seeds and grains that look mouldy, discoloured or shrivelled before preparing them. Cooking or fermenting does not make mouldy nuts safe.
user_text: Throw away mouldy, discoloured or shrivelled nuts and seeds. Cooking does not make them safe.

source: Codex Alimentarius, General Standard for the Labelling of Prepackaged Foods, CXS 1-1985, section 4.2.1.4 ("Peanuts, soybeans and products of these"). Link used: https://vbs.gov.vu/national-standards/images/catalogue/CXS_001e.pdf. Also check each ingredient row allergen_tags.
text: Contains peanut (groundnut) or soya. Peanuts and soybeans are among the foods that cause allergic reactions. Anyone with an allergy to either should not use this ingredient.
user_text: Contains groundnut (peanut) or soya. Do not use if anyone eating is allergic to them.

source: Review "Jack Bean (Canavalia ensiformis L. Abstract only was read. Reviewer: consider turning this into a block and removing jack bean from pantry mode.
text: Jack bean contains toxic compounds (concanavalin A and canavanine). Published detoxification work is mostly on animal feed and finds a residual toxic component even after heat processing. Do not recommend jack bean to households until a food-safety source gives a safe preparation.
user_text: Jack bean has natural toxins and no tested safe home method. Do not cook it for now.
